target_questions.question: Does the method preserve the pressure/velocity jumps and first-order physics needed for shock-induced droplet vaporization?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 1 C031 is the real-fluid phase-change anchor; this paper adds a distinct sharp-interface Riemann-solver method.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: The sharp-interface RS-GFM couples liquid and gas through interfacial pressure/normal-velocity jumps including phase change, surface tension, viscous stress, and Marangoni effects, enabling shock-induced vaporization-rate simulations.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Benchmark validation and 2D/3D shock-droplet simulations demonstrate a complementary numerical representation of first-order interface physics.

limitations: Method-validation study; quantitative vaporization rates remain model- and resolution-dependent.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
